lines.text: 2.6SewageWaste
Sewage is a mixture of both domestic and industrial wastes. It is a major carrier of disease and
toxins.Waste water can originate from both industrial and domestic sources.It contains water,
suspended solids and harmful bacteria that must be removed before the water is released into
streams.
a. Uses of Sewage waste: Sewage waste can be used as an irrigation source due to high organic
this practice.
Sewage must be treated before applying to the fields, as it is rich in high pathogen load, heavy
metals and organic pollutants. The safe treatment of sewage is thus crucial to the health of any
community.
b.Methods of SewageTreatment
The basic methods of sewage treatment are:
i. Physical Method: Physical Method is basically the process of removing small and large floating
sedimentation. Screening removes paper, wood and other large items. Filtration removes
suspended particles or floating particles. The filtered water is then kept in large open tanks
wherethe suspendedimpurities settledown.
i. Biological Method: Biological Method which is the treatment of human waste by bacteria and
micro-organisms thatconvert the sewagewasteintobyproducts suchassludge.
ili. Chemical Method: In a chemical method, chemicals are used to treat waste water. For
example, chlorine and ozone are used to eliminate germs and bacteria.
